thread:
Alexa Chen: FYI there's an enterprise customer (acct: acme-42) reporting invoice > dashboard served tokens after the batcher rollout yesterday. Invoice 0xA12 shows ~18M billed but dashboard shows ~12.7M served. Can we triage?
Raj Patel: grabbing invoice and account now, pinging @billing. Did they observe any error spikes or region failovers?
Alexa Chen: customer says no errors, latency steady. They do heavy streaming chat w/ long prefixes. We rolled continuous-batcher v2 at 03:12 UTC.
billing-bot: Invoice 0xA12 attached (link). Billing counted 17,967,412 token units between 2026-02-28T00:00:00Z and 2026-02-28T23:59:59Z.
Maria Gomez: sounds like the classic metered vs served split where prefetch/prefix caching causes tokens to be metered earlier than 'served' at response time. Did we change prefetch/kvcache behavior in v2?
Sam Liu: quick check of rollout notes: v2 enabled speculative prefetch for continuous batching + relaxed cache eviction. Could cause double-accounting windows.
Raj Patel: what's the instrumentation we can pull quickly? customer wants a short explanation and whether we can credit them.
Maria Gomez: pull trace events from runtime: look for fields metered_tokens and served_tokens in token-telemetry. Example snippet:```json
{"req_id": "r-9a8b7c", "metered_tokens": 1200, "served_tokens": 900, "cache_hit": true, "phase": "prefetch"}
```
Alexa Chen: I have one of their request IDs from logs: r-9a8b7c-20260228. Logged spans show prefetch metering at 00:05:12 and final served at 00:05:13. Metered > served by ~35% on many traces.
Sam Liu: that aligns w/ a scenario where prefetch token accounting increments billing immediately when the token is pulled into KV cache, but served_tokens only counts tokens sent back to client after dedup/eviction. If prefetch is speculative and later evicted, billed tokens remain.
Raj Patel: ok, can engineering produce a report of total prefetch-metered vs final-served per account for that day? that'll show the delta. Also need to check whether our billing pipeline dedups prefetch events.
Maria Gomez: quick query I ran on dev telemetry (simplified):```sql
SELECT sum(metered_tokens) as m, sum(served_tokens) as s FROM token_telemetry WHERE account='acme-42' AND day='2026-02-28';
-- returns m=17967412, s=12702344
```
Alexa Chen: exact numbers match invoice vs dashboard fairly closely. Customer unhappy. They want to know if this is a bug or expected behavior.
Sam Liu: short answer: expected given current accounting semantics — we bill when runtime allocates tokens for inference work (prefetch/kv fill) not strictly when network bytes leave. But v2 rollout changed prefetch aggressiveness so delta jumped.
Raj Patel: customer-facing phrasing please — avoid jargon.
Alexa Chen: suggested message to customer: "We found increased prefetch activity after a recent performance rollout; our billing counts tokens when the runtime reserves work (including prefetches), which can exceed tokens ultimately returned if prefetches are later skipped/evicted. We're investigating options to reduce unnecessary prefetch metering and will propose a remediation/credit." Thoughts?
Maria Gomez: good. Internally, next steps: 1) eng-runtime to produce account-level prefetch vs served delta for 48h window, 2) product/billing to decide credit policy, 3) release a telemetry flag to emit prefetch_reason tag for billing demarcation.
Raj Patel: raised billing ticket BT-7654 and linked invoice + query output. Assigning to @Maria and @Sam for triage.
deploy-bot: Deploy v2-continuous-batcher finished at 2026-02-27T03:12:04Z on pool eu-west-1.
Sam Liu: quick mitigation idea: roll back speculative prefetch flag for that customer or disable prefetch heuristics at customer-account level (config knob exists in Dedicated/Private). Can we flip for acme-42?
Maria Gomez: we can set account config prefetch.enabled=false via admin console for Dedicated/private customers; for hosted we'd need a targeted rollout or rate limit. Acme-42 is hosted. We'll add a per-account override in the runtime config and gate it behind a feature flag; estimate ~3-4 hours to patch and deploy hotfix.
Alexa Chen: customer asking about immediate credit. Billing team: can we offer a one-time adjustment while eng works on a fix?
Raj Patel: provisional one-time credit approved up to $3k pending final reconciliation. I'll log it.
Alexa Chen: Thanks all—I'll update customer now w/ the explanation and that we'll follow up with detailed delta report and a remediation timeline.
Maria Gomez: FYI I scheduled a deeper investigation: looking at KV eviction timing and whether metering events are emitted before eviction decisions. If we can delay metering to commit time we can avoid this class of overcounting, but might impact observability for real-time prefetch billing.
Sam Liu: adding action item: collect sample traces where metered_tokens > served_tokens by >20% and attach to BT-7654. Also add an alert to catch sudden jumps in metered/served ratio per-account.
Alexa Chen: adding to thread: customer asked for repro steps to show on their side. Minimal repro: 1) send long multi-turn chat with repeated overlapping prefixes 2) ensure continuous streaming w/ early prefetch enabled 3) verify dashboard served tokens and compare to invoice timeframe.
Raj Patel: thanks. I'll coordinate credit and close the billing loop once eng shares the report. :thumbsup:
billing-bot: BT-7654 created and linked to Invoice 0xA12.
Alexa Chen: closing loop with customer now, will post updates here.
